problem: RAG for KGQA: recent approaches rely on costly LLM calls to generate executable relation paths or traverse the KG, which is inefficient for complex questions (multi-hop, multi-entity).
method: GNN-RAG. A lightweight GNN scores KG nodes by question relevance and neighbour relevance; shortest paths connecting question entities to GNN answer candidates are retrieved, verbalized, and given to the LLM as context. Additional retrieval-augmentation and routing techniques improve end-to-end efficiency.
key_assumptions: The retrieved question-specific subgraph contains the answer nodes.
Entity linking from the question to KG entities is correct.
Shortest paths from question entities to GNN answer candidates are an adequate verbalized context for the LLM.
main_contribution: Lightweight GNN-based graph retrieval for KGQA that lets a 7B tuned LLM match or outperform GPT-4, improving complex (multi-hop/multi-entity) answering by 8.9-15.5 F1 points over LLM-based retrieval while using 9x fewer KG tokens and no extra LLM calls for retrieval.
baselines: No RAG, KG-RAG variants, long-context inference, GPT-4 (as cited in the abstract)
results: Effective retrieval on WebQSP and CWQ; 8.9-15.5 F1 improvement on multi-hop and multi-entity questions over LLM-based retrieval; 9x fewer KG tokens than long-context inference; matches or beats GPT-4 with a 7B tuned LLM.
limitations: Assumes the KG subgraph the GNN reasons over contains the answer nodes, which may fail for some questions or under entity-linking errors.
Uses simple prompting with shortest paths from question entities to candidate answers as context.
code_availability: Code stated as https://github.com/cmavro/GNN-RAG in the abstract; repository inspection unavailable in this investigation.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: GNN-RAG builds the supporting context (shortest paths) at inference time and feeds it to a frozen/lightly tuned LLM; the supervision used to train the GNN is question-answer pairs, not context-enriched triples. The idea instead attaches co-passage triples to each training supervision signal and compares isolated vs. context regimes, then adds a repair loop and lower-hop RL. Both supply multi-hop context, but one is retrieval-time context construction and the other is training-time supervision enrichment.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.7: both are multi-hop KGQA over the same benchmarks. Method overlap 0.55: retrieval of paths/subgraphs as LLM context is adjacent but is inference-time and path-based, not passage-derived training supervision. Evaluation overlap 0.85: identical WebQSP/CWQ benchmarks and answer-F1-style metrics.
